title: 1080° Avalanche
subtitle: Race down a mountain that will not stay still
summary: 1080° Avalanche is Nintendo Software Technology's snowboarding game, first released for GameCube in Europe on 28 November 2003.
body: 1080° Avalanche is Nintendo Software Technology's snowboarding game, first released for GameCube in Europe on 28 November 2003. The sequel to 1080° Snowboarding emphasises downhill racing, asking the player to reach the finish ahead of a rival while reading the changing slope. Snow, obstacles and turns make the mountain itself part of the contest. Tricks remain available, but maintaining speed through a difficult section can matter more than taking the largest jump when another rider is already approaching the next turn.

The main Match Race mode sends the rider through successive challenges, while Time Trial, Trick Attack and Gate modes give the same control a different purpose. Each rider has individual boards to unlock, allowing the player to vary the equipment used for a run. Four-player split-screen makes the race a direct local contest, and LAN play supports connected GameCube systems. The different modes expose another side of a course, whether the immediate goal is a faster time, a clean route through gates or a higher trick score.

The final event in each Match Race challenge introduces the danger named in the title: an avalanche begins along the route and forces the rider to keep moving ahead of it. The familiar need to preserve speed becomes an urgent escape as the mountain breaks behind the board. Lawrence Schwedler and James Phillipsen composed the original score. These runs give the sequel its most distinctive image, turning the slope from a course to be mastered into a moving threat that follows the rider towards the finish.
